diagnosis.summary: The self-evolution loop is structurally incapable of producing useful evolution. Three distinct design failures are identified: (1) The ROI threshold (>=2.0) is set above the observed ROI (1.75), causing all actions to be silently dropped. (2) The closure log records constant zeros for baseline/new/delta, making it impossible to measure actual improvement. (3) The usage_score Grade B (75/100) is an observability artifact from missing ensemble/ratification corpus components (0/15, 0/10), not an operational failure. All 5 claims (C-001 through C-005) remain unsupported due to missing evidence verification, but the evidence provided is internally consistent and supports the diagnosis.

patches.rationale: The auto-execute threshold (roi >= 2.0 and impact >= 4) is too aggressive. The observed action had roi=1.75 and impact=7, which is a legitimate reliability fix. Lowering the threshold to >=1.5 would allow this action to execute. This is a low-risk config change that can be reverted if it causes issues.

The closure log writes constant zeros for baseline/new/delta. Add a verifier that computes actual performance deltas by comparing pre- and post-action metrics (e.g., tool failure rates, usage scores). This enables meaningful evolution tracking without changing any execution logic.

The tool_failure_aggregation counts detail strings instead of exact tool names for medium signals. Add a verifier that logs the exact tool names alongside detail strings to improve diagnostic accuracy. No behavioral change to existing logic.

The usage_score Grade B is caused by missing ensemble/ratification corpus components (0/15, 0/10). Add a verifier that logs whether these components are expected to exist or are intentionally absent. This prevents false alarms in health checks.

The stale_transient_suppression logic (age>168h or current_ops_healthy() and age>72h) appears reasonable. No change needed. The fix_tool_config handler correctly prints suggestions and logs pending_review without auto-executing. These are appropriate conservative behaviors.
